chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Say: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your Majesty and Your Beauty and Your Generosity that You do for me such and such.'

key_terms.كَذَا وَ كَذَا: Such and such (placeholder for specific request)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for making a personal supplication in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a foundational method of istighatha (seeking help) by anchoring the request in Allah's essential attributes, a practice deeply rooted in Shia tafsir regarding the '99 Names'. It reflects the theological principle that divine generosity (Karam) is intrinsically linked to His majesty, encouraging believers to approach their needs with both reverence and confidence in divine benevolence.
